newsitem.title: UK: LME copper slides below $2,200 in late trading.
newsitem.headline: LME copper slides below $2,200 in late trading.

text.p: Copper prices tumbled below the $2,200 level in late inter-office trading on Friday, compounding losses sustained in a speculative sell-off during afternoon kerb trading.
Traders said the selling spree had flushed out sell-stops that had been lowered, which in turn swept prices to six-month lows.
"The selling gained momentum below $2,256 as stops below $2,250 were triggered," said analyst Martin Squires of brokers Rudolf Wolff.
Three months copper hit a low of $2,185/90 per tonne after finishing the afternoon kerb at $2,213, which was $58 down from Thursday. At 1800 GMT it was indicated just off the lows at $2,193/98.
Below $2,200, the next support level was expected at $2,160/70, analysts said.
Cash to threes, which slid into contango for the first time since September during the kerb, was last bid at a $3 contango.
The other metals were generally a touch softer with copper in late trading, but managed to abstain from similar sell-offs.
Aluminium was last indicated at $1,692/95, versus $1,702 at the kerb close, while zinc was quoted at $1,520/25, compared to $1,525.
